name: Cabbage Thoran
subtitle: shredded cabbage tossed with crushed coconut, mustard and curry leaves

ingredients.note: small Kerala shallots if you can get them

prepNotes: Shred the cabbage as thin as you can — thick shreds steam into limp ribbons instead of staying crisp.
Crush the coconut, garlic, cumin, turmeric and one green chilli together coarsely in a mortar. Do not run it in a blender; you want a rough crumble, not a paste.
Have everything ready by the stove. Thoran is done in fifteen minutes and the tempering waits for nobody.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadhai over medium heat until it thins and shimmers.
Add the mustard seeds and let them pop, about 30 seconds, then add the broken red chillies and curry leaves.
steps.tip: Cover with a lid or a spatter guard — the leaves will crackle hard.

steps.text: Stir in the chopped shallot and remaining slit chillies. Cook 3 minutes until the shallot turns translucent and smells sweet.
Tip in the cabbage and salt. Toss to coat in the oil.
Cover and cook on low for 5 minutes. The cabbage will release its own water — do not add any.
steps.tip: Water is the enemy here. Thoran should be dry, not stewed.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and stir-fry 2 minutes to drive off the moisture at the bottom of the pan.
Add the crushed coconut mixture and toss through for 2 minutes, until the coconut smells toasty and looks dry.
Taste for salt and take it off the heat while the cabbage still has bite.
steps.tip: Overcooked thoran goes grey and sulphurous. Stop early.

storage: Best the day it is made. Keeps 2 days refrigerated; revive in a hot dry pan for 2 minutes rather than a microwave, which makes it watery.
